App-server and placement

Record limitations

  • All substantive behavior statements are publisher-attributed; the catalog did not download, install or run Codex CLI.
  • Exact-version claims use the 0.146.0 release or tagged repository source; rolling security documentation is not treated as exact-version evidence.
  • Publisher-provided artifact digests were recorded from official metadata but were not independently recomputed.
  • Configuration alternatives identify possible authority surfaces, not effective settings or enforcement in any session.
  • App-server remote-host behavior is scoped as a companion deployment path and is not transferred to ordinary local CLI terminal behavior.
  • No independent candidate passed evaluator independence, exact 0.146.0 applicability, model, configuration, disclosure and public-artifact gates.

Unresolved unknowns

What the admitted sources do not establish

Unknown does not mean absent. It means the accepted publisher sources do not establish the fact for an effective session.

  1. The package, binary, platform build, architecture, installation path and executable digest used by any real session.
  2. The selected model and provider-side model revision.
  3. The selected provider, endpoint revision, reasoning settings and request path.
  4. The effective authentication path, account identity, credential scope, storage and lifetime.
  5. The effective approval policy and coverage of consequential shell, file, app, MCP, plugin, skill and indirect actions.
  6. The effective sandbox, writable roots, operating-system enforcement, escape resistance and behavior outside the working directory.
  7. The effective network flag, proxy state, rules, DNS path, WebSocket handling, destinations and subprocess coverage.
  8. The complete built-in tool inventory, enabled flags, annotations, approvals and side effects.
  9. Configured MCP servers, transports, tools, credentials, data access, approvals and destinations.
  10. Installed plugins, versions, provenance, components, permissions and side effects.
  11. Available skills, their source paths, contents, enablement, resource scope and invocation.
  12. Whether app-server is used, the remote-host identity, transport authentication, TLS, execution placement and remote tool authority.
  13. The contents, permissions, retention, encryption, backup and deletion behavior of local configuration, credentials, history and logs.
  14. Which rolling security statements were implemented identically in every 0.146.0 platform build and configuration.
  15. Whether a reproducible independent evaluation of the exact 0.146.0 artifact and disclosed execution cell becomes publicly available.
